summary: Text-box character buffer holder: a heap descriptor at +0x34 and a UTF-16 string with capacity, length and a dirty-flag byte; AppendChars/WriteCharsAt copy characters into it for Ui_TextWidget-style owners.
evidence: Ui_TextBuffer_AppendChars 0x0053F940 and Ui_TextBuffer_WriteCharsAt 0x0053F9EC both guard on f_b4 (buffer present) and f_a4 (u16* data), clamp with the u16 capacity f_cc, update the u16 length f_ce, write a NUL terminator and OR 4 into the byte f_d0. Ui_TextBuffer_Release 0x00548438 frees the tagged pointer at [f_34+4] through virtual slot 0x30 (0x00505040) when both bytes f_51 and f_50 are set. Note: the batch's 'ctor' 0x005487EC is a 0x10-byte unrelated initialiser (writes +0..+0xE only), not this class's constructor.

fields.name: maybe_ownerBlock
fields.evidence: Ui_TextBuffer_Release reads f_34 and treats the word at +4 of the pointed object as a tagged pointer: bit 0 means 'destroy first' (0x0011C814), then 0x00505040 deletes it through vtable slot +0x30 and clears the word; this is a refcounted buffer-owner block, exact type unproven.

fields.name: maybe_hasAllocation
fields.evidence: Release requires f_50 != 0 (together with f_51) before it frees the block and then stores 0 to f_50; name describes 'the buffer currently owns an allocation'.

fields.name: maybe_ownsAllocation
fields.evidence: Release tests f_51 first ('ldrb r0,[r0,#0x51]; ldrbne r0,[r4,#0x50]'); f_51 is never cleared, so it gates whether this object is allowed to free the block at all.

fields.name: textBuffer
fields.evidence: Read as u16* in both writers: 'self->f_a4 + index*2', '*self->f_a4 == 0' and the NUL store '*(u16*)(f_a4 + f_ce*2) = 0'.

fields.name: hasBuffer
fields.evidence: Loaded as a full word before every buffer access ('ldr r0,[r4,#0xb4]; cmp r0,#0'); both writers refuse to touch f_a4 when it is zero, so it is the enable/present flag.

fields.name: bufferCapacity
fields.evidence: AppendChars: 'if (f_cc != 0) limit = f_cc - 1' then clamps the copy to that u16; WriteCharsAt does the same, so f_cc is the capacity in UTF-16 units including the terminator.

fields.name: textLength
fields.evidence: Written as 'index + copied count' after a copy and cleared to 0 when the buffer is empty; the terminator is stored at f_a4 + f_ce*2, i.e. f_ce is the current UTF-16 length.

fields.name: bufferFlags
fields.evidence: Both writers do 'f_d0 |= 4' after changing the string, so bit 2 is a dirty/changed flag; the other bits are never touched in the recovered code.
